dedupe_keys.name: derna libya 2023 dam breaching flood anatomy of a foreseeable disaster

description: This case study analyses the September 2023 flooding in Derna, Libya, where Storm Daniel, a Mediterranean tropical-like cyclone, caused heavy rainfall and the collapse of two embankment dams upstream of the city, with more than 5,000 casualties. Using atmospheric reanalysis, satellite data and hydrologic modelling to overcome data scarcity, the authors found that the return periods of the rainfall and flood were only a few decades, and that hydraulic simulations showed the dam failures amplified damage nearly 20-fold compared with a dam-free scenario. The dams, built since the 1970s, had given a sense of security that encouraged building along the channel and floodplain. The paper argues for uncertainty-aware risk assessment and for distributed flood prevention and early warning, not reliance on single defences. It is published in Science Advances and openly available in PubMed Central. Coverage: the Wadi Derna catchment and the city, one event. Access: free full text; the exact licence was not confirmed on the page read. Caveats: input data were scarce, so the reconstruction relies on reanalysis and satellite rainfall and carries uncertainty. It supports dam-break, cascading failure and flood defence reliability modelling, and relates to the GRanD reservoir and dam database in the catalogue.
